full_text_en:
Huang Zhonghua v. Liu Sanming — dispute over creditor's right of rescission

【Ruling Summary】

Where an employer and an employee reach a compensation agreement regarding a work-related injury, but the agreed compensation amount is significantly lower than the work-related injury insurance benefits to which the employee is entitled, it shall be deemed as grossly unfair. If the employee requests to rescind such compensation agreement, the people's court shall support the claim.

Plaintiff: Huang Zhonghua, female, 39 years old, Han ethnicity, farmer, residing at Malan Village, Penglai Town, Daying County, Sichuan Province.

Defendant: Liu Sanming, male, 39 years old, Han ethnicity, individual business operator, owner of Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory.

The plaintiff, Huang Zhonghua, filed a lawsuit with the Guanghan People's Court of Sichuan Province against the defendant, Liu Sanming, concerning a dispute over creditor's right of rescission.

Plaintiff Huang Zhonghua alleged: The plaintiff was a worker at Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory and was injured at work on July 17, 2009. On August 3, 2009, Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory applied for a work-related injury determination for the plaintiff's injury. On August 4, 2009, before the conclusion of the work-related injury determination and the labor ability appraisal, the plaintiff and Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory entered into an unfair compensation agreement that harmed the plaintiff's lawful rights and interests. Subsequently, upon appraisal, the plaintiff was determined to have a Grade 10 disability. The plaintiff repeatedly demanded that the defendant, Liu Sanming, compensate for the losses caused by the work-related injury in accordance with the law, but the defendant refused to pay. The plaintiff requested the court to rescind the compensation agreement signed with Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory on August 4, 2009.

Defendant Liu Sanming argued: The compensation agreement signed on August 4, 2009, had already been performed. The plaintiff, Huang Zhonghua, is a person with full capacity for civil conduct. The agreement was voluntarily signed by both parties without gross misunderstanding or gross unfairness, and thus the agreement is valid. The defendant requested the court to dismiss the plaintiff's claim.

The Guanghan People's Court found the following facts at first instance:

The defendant, Liu Sanming, is an individual business operator and the owner of Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory. The plaintiff, Huang Zhonghua, worked at Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory. At 3:10 p.m. on July 17, 2009, the plaintiff was injured while working and was treated at Guanghan Orthopedic Hospital and Guanghan People's Hospital. Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory prepaid the medical expenses. On August 3, 2009, Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory applied to the Deyang Municipal Bureau of Labor and Social Security for a work-related injury determination for the plaintiff's injury. On August 4, 2009, the plaintiff was discharged from the hospital. On the same day, the plaintiff and Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory reached a compensation agreement regarding the work-related injury accident. The agreement did not bear the defendant's official seal but was signed by Liu Zhangming, the production manager of Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory, on behalf of the factory. On the day the agreement was signed, the plaintiff received from the factory a lump-sum disability subsidy, lump-sum employment and medical subsidy for disability, and lump-sum nursing fee totaling RMB 4,000, and issued a receipt. On August 21, 2009, the Deyang Municipal Bureau of Labor and Social Security accepted the defendant's application for work-related injury determination and issued a work-related injury determination on October 10 of the same year. On February 9, 2010, upon appraisal by the Deyang Municipal Labor Ability Appraisal Committee, Huang Zhonghua was determined to have a Grade 10 disability. On May 11, 2010, Huang Zhonghua applied to the Guanghan Labor Dispute Arbitration Committee for arbitration to declare the compensation agreement invalid. On May 11, 2010, the Guanghan Labor Dispute Arbitration Committee issued a decision of non-acceptance and served a notice of non-acceptance to Huang Zhonghua.

It was also found that the agreement between the parties stipulated: "...Party B voluntarily waives the work-related injury determination and disability grade appraisal. Through friendly negotiation between Party A and Party B, the agreement is reached as follows: 1. In addition to the medical expenses, wages during the period of suspension of work, transportation expenses, and hospitalization subsidies totaling RMB 2,927.92 already paid by Party A, Party A shall pay Party B a lump-sum disability subsidy, lump-sum employment and medical subsidy for disability, lump-sum nursing fee, etc., totaling RMB 4,000. 2. Both parties voluntarily terminate the labor relationship on the date of signing this agreement. Party A shall pay the above amount to Party B in a lump sum on the date of signing this agreement, and Party B shall issue a receipt to Party A. All economic dealings between Party A and Party B regarding this matter are fully settled. 3. Party A and Party B sign this agreement to make a one-time settlement of this matter. Party B guarantees that it will not, for any reason, make any further economic claims against Party A regarding this matter..."

The issues in dispute at first instance were: 1. Whether the nature of the case was a labor dispute or a dispute over the right of rescission; 2. Whether the agreement signed by the parties constituted an act subject to rescission.

The Guanghan People's Court held at first instance:

In this case, the plaintiff, Huang Zhonghua, requested the rescission of the compensation agreement, which did not involve the substantive handling of work-related injury compensation. Therefore, the nature of the case should be a dispute over the right of rescission rather than a labor dispute. Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory is an individual business operated by Liu Sanming, so the defendant should be Liu Sanming himself, not Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory. The plaintiff was injured while working at Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory, and the relevant liability arising therefrom should be borne by the defendant. After Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory applied to the Deyang Municipal Bureau of Labor and Social Security for a work-related injury determination, the plaintiff and Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory reached an agreement on compensation. Although the agreement did not bear the official seal of Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory, it was signed by Liu Zhangming, a representative recognized by Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory. Liu Zhangming's signing was an act performed in the course of his duties, and the rights and obligations under the agreement were assumed by Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory. The content of the agreement did not violate national laws and regulations and was established and became effective upon signing by both parties. Since Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory had already submitted an application for work-related injury determination to the Deyang Municipal Bureau of Labor and Social Security, the plaintiff voluntarily waived the work-related injury determination and disability grade appraisal and made a one-time settlement with Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory regarding compensation. The agreement reflected the true intentions of both parties and was binding on the parties. The plaintiff is a person with full capacity for civil conduct and must bear legal responsibility for her own decisions. It should be determined that the parties signed the agreement after full consultation and voluntarily, and there was no gross misunderstanding, gross unfairness, or other statutory grounds for rescission as provided in Article 54 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. The plaintiff's application for disability grade appraisal and the subsequent determination of Grade 10 disability could not overturn the fact that the parties had already reached a compensation agreement and performed it. Therefore, the plaintiff's claim should not be supported.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 44, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 2, Paragraph 2 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the Guanghan People's Court rendered the following judgment on October 26, 2010:

The plaintiff Huang Zhonghua's claim is dismissed.

Huang Zhonghua, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Deyang Intermediate People's Court, arguing: 1. In the first instance, the appellant had sued Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory under the cause of action of dispute over compensation for work-related injury damages. The Guanghan People's Court arbitrarily changed the defendant to Liu Sanming and changed the cause of action to dispute over the right of rescission, seriously infringing upon the appellant's lawful rights and interests. 2. The appellant was unaware that the appellee, Liu Sanming, had submitted an application for work-related injury determination. Therefore, the Guanghan People's Court's finding that "the plaintiff voluntarily waived the work-related injury determination and disability grade appraisal since Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory had already submitted an application for work-related injury determination to the Deyang Municipal Bureau of Labor and Social Security" was erroneous in fact. 3. The various compensations to which the appellant was entitled by law for a Grade 10 disability should be around RMB 50,000. The signed agreement was grossly unfair and violated mandatory legal norms, concealing illegal purposes in a lawful form, and should be invalid.

The appellee, Liu Sanming, argued: 1. The appellant's claim in the first instance was to rescind the agreement signed by both parties. The court had the right to determine that this case was a contract dispute based on the content of the claim. 2. If this case were a labor dispute, the business name could be used as the party. However, since this case is a contract dispute, only the owner can be the party. 3. Invalid contract and voidable contract are two different concepts. The validity of the contract should be examined by the court, and the appellant failed to provide evidence to prove that the agreement was grossly unfair. Therefore, the Guanghan People's Court correctly found the facts and applied the law, and the appellee requested that the appeal be dismissed and the first-instance judgment be affirmed.

Upon second instance, the Deyang Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The issues in dispute at second instance were: 1. Whether the nature of the case was a dispute over compensation for work-related injury damages or a dispute over creditor's right of rescission, and the determination of the parties; 2. Whether the compensation agreement signed by the parties violated mandatory provisions and constituted gross unfairness.

The Deyang Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

First, regarding the nature of the case and the defendant party. The nature of a civil case shall be determined based on the nature of the civil legal relationship asserted by the parties. In the first instance, the party requested the rescission of the compensation agreement reached for the work-related injury damages, but the claim did not involve the substantive handling of work-related injury compensation. Therefore, the nature of the case was a dispute over the creditor's right of rescission under the category of contract disputes. Article 9 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases (II) provides: "In a labor dispute lawsuit between an employee and an individual business operator that has a trade name, the people's court shall treat the trade name registered on the business license as the party, but shall also indicate the natural status of the owner of the trade name." Article 41 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (For Trial Implementation) provides: "For an individual business operator that has a trade name, in civil litigation, the household head (owner) registered on the business license shall be the party to the litigation, and the litigation documents shall indicate that the party is the household head of a certain trade name." In this case, the compensation agreement reached by the parties for the work-related injury damages has the general attributes of a contract. Therefore, it was not inappropriate for the Guanghan People's Court to handle this case as a general civil proceeding and treat the owner, Liu Sanming, as the party, and it did not harm the lawful rights and interests of the parties.

Second, regarding the validity of the compensation agreement. Article 10 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases (III) provides: "If an employee and an employer reach an agreement on matters such as handling procedures for termination or dissolution of the labor contract, payment of wages, remuneration, overtime pay, economic compensation, or damages, and the agreement does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations and does not involve fraud, duress, or exploitation of the other party's difficulties, the agreement shall be deemed valid. If the agreement in the preceding paragraph involves gross misunderstanding or gross unfairness, and a party requests its rescission, the people's court shall support the claim." In this case, the compensation agreement reached by the parties for the work-related injury damages did not violate the mandatory norms of laws or regulations. The appellant's ground for appeal that the agreement violated mandatory provisions cannot be sustained.

Regarding whether the agreement signed by the parties constituted gross unfairness. So-called gross unfairness means that the rights and obligations of the parties are obviously unequal, causing one party to suffer substantial adverse consequences. The constituent elements are: the rights and obligations of the parties are obviously unequal; this inequality violates the principle of fairness and exceeds the limit permitted by law; and it is not caused by fraud, duress, exploitation of the other party's difficulties, malicious collusion, or other reasons harming the interests of others. In this case, the appellant, Huang Zhonghua, had a Grade 10 disability. The lump-sum disability subsidy she was entitled to was 7 months of her personal wages, and the lump-sum medical subsidy and employment subsidy for disability (10 months of the average wage of the overall planning area in the previous year). The total compensation paid by the appellee, Liu Sanming, to the appellant was RMB 6,927.92 (including medical expenses), which was significantly lower than the work-related injury insurance benefits to which the appellant was entitled. Furthermore, ordinary contract relationships only involve disputes over property rights between the parties. However, in this case, although the compensation agreement reached by the parties for the work-related injury damages has the general attributes of a contract, the handling of this case does not concern a simple creditor-debtor relationship but involves the survival rights and interests of the employee. Therefore, considering all the above factors, the court held that the compensation agreement signed by the parties resulted in unequal rights and obligations, causing Huang Zhonghua to suffer substantial detriment, and thus constituted gross unfairness.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 10 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases (III) and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Deyang Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on July 16, 2011:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2010) Guanghan Min Chu Zi No. 920 of Guanghan People's Court;

2. Set aside the compensation agreement signed between Appellant Huang Zhonghua and Guanghan Yida Plywood Processing Factory owned by Appellee Liu Sanming.

This judgment is final.
